query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Minor Al enrichment will raise the room-temperature coercive field of a face–centred-cubic (FCC) CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy because Al triggers nanoscale ordered precipitates that pin domain walls.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy produced by arc-melting and homogenised (single-phase FCC, grain size ≈20 µm, Hc ≈50 Oe at 300 K).
generation.intervention: Add 2 at.% Al (CoCrFeNiAl0.02) followed by 70 % cold-rolling and annealing at 600 °C for 1 h in Ar.
generation.conditions: Magnetic hysteresis measured at 300 K in out-of-plane field up to ±10 kOe on bulk samples of identical thickness and surface finish.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of 5–20 nm L1_0-like (Co,Fe)Al-rich ordered precipitates uniformly dispersed in the FCC matrix and a concomitant dislocation/strain field retained from the moderate anneal.
generation.mechanism: Nanoscale ordered precipitates and residual strain act as strong pinning centres for domain walls and raise the effective magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy, leading to a higher coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Al-modified alloy will show a coercive field at least 25 % higher than the Al-free baseline (e.g., ≥65 Oe vs. 50 Oe) under the stated conditions, without a significant drop (>5 %) in saturation magnetisation.
generation.baseline: Coercive field of the Al-free CoCrFeNi processed identically except for Al addition (cold-rolled 70 %, 600 °C/1 h anneal).
generation.boundary: Effect expected only for low Al additions (≤4 at.%) and annealing temperatures between 500–700 °C; higher Al or higher annealing temperatures allow precipitate coarsening and FCC-to-B2 transition that may reduce coercivity or alter magnetic phase.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of Hc increase is uncertain because particle size, number density and retained strain depend sensitively on processing; outcome may vary if precipitates over-coarsen or if Al alters overall magnetic moment unfavorably.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys (baseline CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiAl0.02) via identical melting, cold-rolling 70 %, and 600 °C/1 h anneal. Measure grain size (EBSD), precipitate size/density (TEM), and hysteresis loops (VSM).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the average Hc of the Al-modified alloy is not at least 25 % higher than that of the baseline, while Ms differs by <5 %, the hypothesis is falsified.
